items.text: Proposition 122 (the Natural Medicine Health Act, passed in November 2022) decriminalised personal possession and use of psilocybin for adults 21 and over, and set up licensed healing centers where sessions are supervised by a licensed facilitator. Businesses can't sell psilocybin outside that program.
The state issued its first healing center licence in 2025, in Denver.

laws.rule: Adults 21 and over may buy and possess up to 1 ounce at a time from licensed stores. Any public use (smoking, eating or vaping) is illegal, including on sidewalks, in parks, ski resorts, concert venues, businesses, restaurants and bars, and building common areas. Cannabis remains illegal under US federal law, including on federal land such as national parks.

Using cannabis in public is illegal, including on sidewalks, in parks, at ski resorts, concert venues, bars and restaurants. It is also illegal on federal land such as national parks and forests, and taking cannabis out of Colorado or into any airport is illegal.

Colorado Parks and Wildlife's rules for state parks (Chapter P-1) allow drinking alcohol on its lands with exceptions: not on archery or firearm ranges unless a contract or permit says so; selling or dispensing needs a concession contract or permit; and being on the land so affected by alcohol or a controlled substance that you endanger people, property or resources is prohibited. Individual parks can be stricter.

Under Colorado's state park rules (Chapter P-1), fires are allowed only in designated sites in park-furnished grills or fireplaces, or in hibachis, charcoal grills, stoves and other metal containers, and must be fully extinguished; all fires may be prohibited as posted for burn restrictions. Some places ban fires entirely, such as Roxborough State Park and Highline Canal State Trail. Possessing or discharging fireworks is prohibited (display approved by the Director excepted), and carrying glassware inside a public swimming or bathing area or designated water-ski beach is not allowed.

access.opening: Park open daily year-round, no entry reservation needed. Wetherill Mesa is closed for the season (reopens late spring); the Mesa Verde Museum is closed for renovation from 25 October 2026 until late spring 2027.
access.tickets: Private vehicle, 7 days: US$30 (about A$42.61 at the RBA rate of 30 October 2026) from 1 May to 31 October, US$20 (about A$28.41 at the RBA rate of 30 October 2026) from 1 November to 30 April. Per person on foot or bike (16 and over) US$15 (about A$21.31 at the RBA rate of 30 October 2026). The fees page does not mention a non-resident surcharge.

layers.process: 2026 timed entry, booked on recreation.gov in 2-hour entry windows (stay as long as you like once in). Timed Entry (without Bear Lake Road): 9 am to 2 pm daily, 22 May to Monday 12 Oct. Timed Entry plus Bear Lake Road: 5 am to 6 pm daily, 22 May to Sunday 18 Oct. Release at 8 am MDT: 1 May (22 May to 30 Jun), 1 Jun (July), 1 Jul (August), 1 Aug (September), 1 Sep (1 to 18 Oct); extra reservations release at 7 pm MDT the night before. Fee: US$2 (about A$2.80) non-refundable booking fee per reservation; a park entrance fee or pass is needed at all times. Campers at Aspenglen, Glacier Basin and Moraine Park, wilderness permit holders, horse-ride bookings, permitted commercial operators and cyclists are covered or exempt as listed. Outside the hours no reservation is needed. A separate Hiker Shuttle ticket is not a timed entry. Fees in US dollars; A$1 = USD 0.7040 (RBA, 30 Oct 2026), so US$1 is about A$1.42.
